An algorithm with bundled access could run it with the same seed and transcript using at most $B_{\rm first}+B_{\rm HVP}$ bundled calls. Apply Appendix F. For $\kappa\ge6$, the lift uses $b^2=(\kappa-3)/2$ and turns $\varepsilon$ primal stationarity into single-level stationarity at $3\varepsilon/(2b)$. The all-derivative lower bound has scale $\min\{A_1,A_2\}=A_2$ in the stated window. One preliminary source query for the affine offset can be absorbed for $A_2\ge C_0$. Each block is padded to its requested dimension, using an inert primal block and a known $\mu_y$-quadratic dual block. The hard instances start with exact inner maximization and therefore obey every $R_y\ge0$ promise.

proofs.proof: Retain exactly the frozen model, public initial point, x-only output, success guarantee and nonnegative pathwise resource caps. Write y_x=y^star(x). Strong concavity implies mu_y ||y_x-y_x'|| <= ||grad_y f(x,y_x')-grad_y f(x',y_x')|| <= beta ||x-x'||, using the two zero dual gradients and strong monotonicity; the conclusion also holds when the dual points coincide. Hence ||y_x-y_x'|| <= kappa ||x-x'||. The frozen reduced-gradient identity then gives ||grad Phi(x)-grad Phi(x')|| <= beta (||x-x'||+||y_x-y_x'||) <= L ||x-x'||, L=beta(1+kappa)>0. For g=grad Phi(x0), s=-g/L, integrate the gradient along the segment: Phi(x0+s)-Phi(x0)=int_0^1 <grad Phi(x0+t s),s> dt <= <g,s>+L||s||^2/2=-||g||^2/(2L). Since inf Phi <= Phi(x0+s), ||g||^2 <= 2L(Phi(x0)-inf Phi) <= 2 beta(1+kappa) Delta. Under the closed predicate Z this is <=epsilon^2. The algorithm returns the already public x0 without calls, so it succeeds on every instance with probability one and has fixed pathwise cap (0,0). No y^star computation, reduced-gradient oracle or certificate is required by the algorithm. Resource nonnegativity makes (0,0) the exact minimal pair and every nonnegative pair attainable on Z. This is a sufficient endpoint, not a converse threshold. It is uniform in all nine native tracked parameters. It does not constrain rho or R_y beyond the contract. For consistency with the retained lower window H, Z implies A1<=1/[2(1+kappa)], and r<=1 implies A2=A1 sqrt(r)<=A1. With kappa>=6 this gives A2<=1/14<C0 for sufficiently large universal C0>=1, so Z and H are disjoint.
